title: “WHERE YOU GO, I WILL GO.”
paragraphs: “WHERE YOU GO, I WILL GO.”

Four words.
But they sounded like an earthquake.

A young widow…
Standing at a dusty crossroads…
About to abandon everything she had ever known.

Her language.
Her land.
Her gods.
Her future.
Gone.
This is the moment in Book of Ruth chapter 1 when Ruth the Moabite looked at her broken mother-in-law, Naomi, and made one of the most radical vows ever spoken by a human heart.
Not romantic love.
Covenant love.
Naomi had nothing left.

Her husband dead.
Her sons buried.
Her future empty.
Three graves in a foreign land.
So Naomi told her daughters-in-law the hard truth:

“Go home. Start over. I have nothing to give you.”
(Ruth 1:11–13)
One daughter-in-law kissed Naomi goodbye.
But Ruth?
She gripped Naomi tighter.
Then she spoke words that still thunder across history:

“Do not urge me to leave you…
Where you go I will go.
Where you stay I will stay.
Your people will be my people,
and your God my God.”
— Ruth 1:16
Pause there.
Ruth wasn’t just changing addresses.
She was abandoning Moab — a land of idols — to follow the living God of Yahweh.
She chose faith over familiarity.
She chose God over comfort.
She chose loyalty over survival.
And she had no idea what it would cost.
Or what it would lead to.
Here’s the shock.

This foreign widow…
This outsider…
This immigrant woman with nothing…
Would become the great-grandmother of King David.
And generations later…
Her bloodline would carry the Savior of the world.
Jesus Christ.
Think about that.
A Moabite widow…
woven into the genealogy of the Messiah.
Grace does that.
God writes redemption in places people expect rejection.
Some of you are standing at Ruth’s crossroads right now.
Following Christ might cost you comfort.

Maybe reputation.
Maybe relationships.
Maybe the future you planned.
But the road that looks like loss…
…can become the road that leads straight into the purposes of God.
Ruth walked away from everything.
And walked straight into redemption.
Friend, the Gospel is this:
We were outsiders too.

Foreign to God.
Broken by sin.
Hopeless on our own.
But Jesus came to bring us home.

Through His cross, strangers become family.
Through His grace, the rejected become heirs.

No past is too far.
No story too ruined.
If God can weave Ruth into the story of Christ…
He can rewrite yours too.
🔥 Question for you:

What is God asking you to leave behind
so you can follow Him fully?
Because sometimes the holiest step you’ll ever take…
is walking away from the old life.
Toward God.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
